_note: An illustrative schedule for the timeline. The model assumes only twelve years of works with even spending (params.build_years); the split of those years between tasks and stages is an assumption made for this page, not a programme.

Tunnels: north, east, Nord-Est to Lyon, southeast
Shafts, work sites, moving pipes and cables
Halls refitted: Gare du Nord, Gare de l’Est, Gare de Lyon
Surface tracks closed, north, east and southeast

network.text: Every train ends in Paris. Changing from one line to another means crossing the city by metro or RER.
Trains from the north, the east and the southeast stop at Paris Nord-Est; those of the southeast also stop at Gare de Lyon. Some run straight through Paris. Atlantic trains still end at Montparnasse.
The four lines are joined. Every train stops at Paris Nord-Est, and most trains stop twice in Paris.

seen.name: Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est

phases.text: Trains run as today. Work sites appear on railway land beside the approach tracks. Some entrances and passages are moved.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are shortened or closed in turn above the works, and some trains leave from other platforms.
The station below is complete; empty trains run through it. New ways down appear in the two halls, still closed.
Trains leave from the deep platforms. The two halls are the entrances. London trains use the sealed platforms. The surface platforms close and the halls are refitted.
One station with two halls. The surface tracks are closed; their land can be handed over.
A terminal on two levels: main-line trains above, RER below.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear beside the tracks towards Bercy.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works.
Empty trains run through the station below. New ways down appear in the hall, still closed.
Trains leave from the deep platforms and continue to Paris Nord-Est. The surface platforms close and the hall is refitted.
The hall is the entrance. The tracks towards Bercy are closed; their land can be handed over.
A terminal with platforms one level above the street.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear beside the approach tracks.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works.
All Atlantic trains still end here on the surface, while the other three lines are already joined. Below, the station is being fitted out.
Empty trains run through the station below. New ways down appear in the hall, still closed.
Trains leave from the deep platforms and continue to Paris Nord-Est. The surface platforms and the tracks to the ring road close.
